judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 5 Indicators (same statement-type grain, rank 1) under the same B5.1.1.1 place-value Content Standard in Number / Counting, Representation & Cardinality. B5.1.1.1.2 (LCs: read numbers in figures and words up to 1000,000; write numbers in figures and words up to 1000,000) establishes fluent recognition and notation of multi-digit numerals, which substantively supports B5.1.1.1.4 (LCs: compare whole numbers up to 100,000; order whole numbers up to 100,000; represent the comparison using '>, <, or ='), where learners must interpret multi-digit numerals to judge relative magnitude and encode that judgement symbolically. The developmental step is from naming/notating numerals to relating them by magnitude and representing those relations, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first; same-rank direction rests on this skill-content dependency, not on code order or page proximity alone. Evidence limits: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the shared Content Standard parent carries a merge decision for a stale 'CONT'D' duplication, so hierarchy is used only as supporting context.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same grain, rank 1) under Content Standard B5.1.1.1 'Demonstrate an understanding of quantities and place value for multi-digit numerals up to 1000,000' in Strand 1-Number, Sub-strand Counting, Representation & Cardinality. The second SFI (B5.1.1.1.1) has learners model number quantities up to 1,000,000 with graph sheets and multi-base blocks, building concrete place-value structure (LC tags 'place value', 'modelling', 'multi-base block'). The first SFI (B5.1.1.1.5) requires rounding off/up/down whole numbers up to 100,000 to the nearest ten thousands, thousands, hundreds and tens, which presupposes fluency in identifying and comparing place-value positions; its LCs are also tagged 'place value'. Proficiency in representing/modelling multi-digit quantities therefore supports success in place-value-dependent rounding, a substantive same-rank developmental direction rather than mere shared parent or code-prefix overlap. Direction asserted at same rank on this conceptual dependency, not on source code order; evidence for both endpoints is bounded by truncated source excerpts and upstream merge context on the shared Content Standard and Grade organizers, which tempers confidence.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Content Standards (same statement-type grain, same coordinate rank 1) under Strand 3 Geometry and Measurement, but in different sub-strands: B5.3.1.1 (Lines and Shapes) identifies and sorts quadrilaterals by attributes, while B5.3.2.1 (Measurement) estimates and measures perimeter and surface area of 2-D shapes in centimetre/metre. The two are substantively coherent — the 2-D shapes measured in B5.3.2.1 are the very quadrilaterals classified in B5.3.1.1, so attribute knowledge (sides, dimensions) reinforces measurement work and vice versa. However, within the same grade rank the evidence shows no substantive developmental dependency: perimeter/surface-area estimation and calculation is framed around measurement referents and computation rather than on prior classification, and the supporting nomination signals (code prefix 'b5.3', page proximity, token overlap limited to 'and') are weak and non-semantic. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment rather than a directional buildsTowards.

The relationship is complementary reinforcement of factor reasoning within one standard, i.e. relatesTo. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators (same statement-type grain) in Strand 'Geometry and Measurement'. The BASIC 4 indicator (rank 0, B4.3.3.1.1) has learners estimate perimeter using personal referents for centimetre or metre, establishing the idea of a referent for a standard measurement unit in one dimension. The BASIC 5 indicator (rank 1, B5.3.2.2.1) extends the same referent reasoning to three-dimensional cubic units (cm3 or m3) under the volume Content Standard and adds justification of the chosen referent. This is a substantive extension from linear to cubic units and from estimating to selecting-and-justifying, so proficiency with length referents supports success with volume referents; direction is lower-to-higher rank (BASIC 4 -> BASIC 5), i.e. second_to_first. Shared 'referents' wording plus the sub-strand/measurement context, not code prefixes alone, supports this. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), and both sides carry merge/same-code audit context, so exemplar detail beyond the bounded excerpts is unavailable.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 4 Indicators (rank 0, same Grade coordinate) within Strand 1: NUMBER, Sub-strand 2: Number Operations, but under different Content Standards: B4.1.2.1 'Recall basic multiplication fact up to 12 × 12' (first) and B4.1.2.4 'Recall basic division fact up to 100' (second). The first requires determining basic multiplication facts up to 12 × 12; the second requires determining basic division facts up to 81, i.e. the inverse-operation facts drawn from the same multiplication-table domain (81 = 9 × 9 within the 12 × 12 grid). Fluency with multiplication facts substantively supports determining the corresponding division facts, which is a pair-specific developmental dependency rather than mere shared wording ('basic', 'determine', 'up to') or shared ancestry/code prefix. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (rank 1, gap 0) under the same Content Standard B5.3.1.1 (sorting quadrilaterals by attributes), Sub-Strand 'Lines and Shapes'. B5.3.1.1.2 has learners use paper folding with cut-out squares and rectangles to investigate side, angle and diagonal properties; its LCs are investigative ('investigate the properties of the sides/angles/diagonals of squares and rectangles'). B5.3.1.1.3 applies the same folding technique plus measurement of sides and angles to prove a polygon is regular ('prove that a polygon is regular by folding and superimposing'; 'by measuring the sides and angles'). This is a substantive same-rank progression: from hands-on exploration of side/angle properties in specific quadrilaterals to using those property criteria as a justification/proof argument generalised to polygons, so proficiency in the folding investigation supports success in the proving task. Direction is not merely code or page order; the shift from investigate-to-prove and specific-to-general provides pair-specific evidence. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), which limits but does not contradict this reading.
